20261118-chemistry-g11.material: [H2 Chemistry Inquiry] Inquiry problem on First Steps in Chemistry and the Mole. At $25^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\text{ atm}$, the molar volume of a gas is $24.5\text{ L/mol}$. Under the same conditions, what is the volume in $\text{L}$ of $0.2\text{ mol}$ of this gas?
20261118-chemistry-g11.thinking.0: First Steps in Chemistry and the Mole
20261118-chemistry-g11.s.s1.prompt: [H2 Chemistry Inquiry] Inquiry problem on First Steps in Chemistry and the Mole. At $25^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\text{ atm}$, the molar volume of a gas is $24.5\text{ L/mol}$. Under the same conditions, what is the volume in $\text{L}$ of $0.2\text{ mol}$ of this gas?
20261118-chemistry-g11.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: By Avogadro's law, gas volume $V$ is directly proportional to moles $n$.
Step 2: $V = n \times V_m = 0.2\text{ mol} \times 24.5\text{ L/mol}$.
Step 3: Calculating yields $V = 4.90\text{ L}$.
20261118-chemistry-g11.s.s1.hint.0: Under constant T and P, gas volume is directly proportional to moles.

20261121-chemistry-g11-1.material: [H2 Chemistry Inquiry (Advanced)] Quantitative analysis problem on First Steps in Chemistry and the Mole. Acidic solution $A$ has $[\text{H}^+] = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$ and solution $B$ has $[\text{H}^+] = 1.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ M}$. How many times greater is the hydrogen ion concentration of $A$ than $B$?
20261121-chemistry-g11-1.thinking.0: First Steps in Chemistry and the Mole
20261121-chemistry-g11-1.s.s1.prompt: [H2 Chemistry Inquiry (Advanced)] Quantitative analysis problem on First Steps in Chemistry and the Mole. Acidic solution $A$ has $[\text{H}^+] = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$ and solution $B$ has $[\text{H}^+] = 1.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ M}$. How many times greater is the hydrogen ion concentration of $A$ than $B$?
20261121-chemistry-g11-1.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: $[\text{H}^+]_A = 10^{-3}\text{ M}$, $[\text{H}^+]_B = 10^{-5}\text{ M}$.
Step 2: $\frac{1.0 \times 10^{-3}}{1.0 \times 10^{-5}} = 10^{-3 - (-5)} = 10^2 = 100$.
Step 3: Solution $A$ has 100 times higher $[\text{H}^+]$ than solution $B$.
